understanding.bridge: What you call wanting it all to end is the mind's way of screaming that it has nowhere to go.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from the thought that you could vanish to the first moment of being seen again.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the thought that no one would notice, named without judgement.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that it is the disconnection, not your worth, that is speaking so loudly.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the self that is real cannot be lost by anyone.
week_beats.act: You try reaching out to one person and naming what you feel, and letting the mind run without fighting it.
week_beats.story: A young seeker who felt abandoned found that the self was never gone, and that is where they began again.

understanding.core_struggle: A young student feels erased and is thinking of ending it, believing no one would notice if they were gone.
understanding.mirror: It sounds like you're carrying something very heavy right now.
understanding.insight: What you're carrying is heavy, and it is not a measure of your worth. You don't have to carry it alone.

queries.hook: When the darkness feels endless and the heart is too tired to go on, and no one seems to see the pain.
queries.diagnose: When the heart is cut off from people and purpose, the mind turns on itself; the thought that no one would notice is the deepest loneliness, not the truth.
queries.steady: This darkness is a passing night, not the whole of you; the self within you is whole, held and never alone.
queries.act: Hold on through the dark night and reach out to someone who cares; the self within you is not broken and is never alone.
queries.story: A young seeker who felt abandoned by the world, questioned everything, and found that the self was never gone.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
verse.line: Out of compassion, I live in their hearts and clear the darkness with the lamp of understanding.
verse.translation: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
verse.why: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

prasang.title: The yoga of devotion and its fruit
prasang.summary: Devotees talk of the divine with each other and find joy; out of compassion Krishna lights the lamp of knowledge in their hearts.
prasang.lesson: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about the people who gather and talk about him. They find joy in each other's company. Out of compassion for them, he lives inside their hearts. He clears the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
verse.for_you: You feel erased and think no one would notice. But your mind is not a void. It is a room where a lamp is waiting to be lit. The noise you hear is the dark asking for light.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing that feels real today.
verse.scene_line: You are in a dark room waiting for a lamp to turn on.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.for_you: You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama, ending his lament, says where he still sees hope.
verse.sanskrit: विद्यन्त एवेह न ते महात्मन् दुराधयो न क्षयमाप्नुवन्ति । ये सङ्गमेनोत्तममानसानां निशातमांसीव निशाकरेण ॥
verse.line: There is no trouble that good people's company can't ease, as moonlight eases the night.
verse.translation: Great sage, there are no troubles in the world that do not fade through the company of noble-minded people, as the darkness of night fades before the moon.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.meaning: Rama, after telling his elders how life slips away and how the mind never fills, ends his speech by naming a single place of hope. He says that no trouble in the world can withstand the company of good people, just as the dark of night fades before the moon comes up. The verse does not say the trouble disappears. It says the darkness lifts when someone else is there with you. The point is that your emptiness is seen and held by others, even when it feels like it is only yours.
verse.for_you: You are in a room where the walls feel like they are closing in, and the phone is the only window. But the screen is not the whole world. The verse says that the dark does not last when someone good is near.
verse.try_today: Send one message to a friend or mentor, even if you have nothing to say.
verse.scene_line: You are in the dark of your own room, and the moon of a friend's voice is about to rise.

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: Describing the one Lord who pervades all, the seer adds what he is to each of us.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितम् । सर्वस्य प्रभुमीशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥
verse.line: The Lord of everything is also everyone's refuge and everyone's friend.
verse.translation: He shines through the powers of all the senses yet has no senses; he is the master and ruler of all, the refuge of all, the friend of all.
verse.why: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

prasang.title: Shvetashvatara: from 'what governs our lives?' to refuge
prasang.summary: Seekers ask what causes the world and governs their joys and sorrows. Through meditation they come to see one Lord, Rudra-Shiva, hidden in every heart; the Upanishad moves from inquiry to recognition to a prayer of refuge (6.18) and ends on grace and love of God (6.21, 6.23).
prasang.lesson: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

verse.meaning: The Seer tells the seekers that the one Lord who governs all is also the refuge and friend of everyone. He shines through all our senses but has no senses of his own. He is the master and ruler of everything, the one you can go to for shelter and the one who walks beside you as a friend.
verse.for_you: You feel erased because your mind is spinning and you believe no one would notice you gone. The verse says the Lord of everything is the refuge and friend of everyone.
verse.try_today: Notice one small thing in your room and let it be your friend for a moment.
verse.scene_line: You are the seeker in the dark, and the Lord is the light that does not leave.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram to Sugriva on what a friend actually does.
verse.sanskrit: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥
verse.line: A friend steers you off the wrong path, speaks of your strengths, and keeps your faults private.
verse.translation: Why do those who lack this natural feeling force themselves into friendships? A friend turns you back from the wrong path and sets you on the right one, makes your good qualities known and keeps your faults to himself.
verse.why: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.
verse.misuse: Keeping faults private means discretion, not covering up harm.

prasang.title: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

verse.meaning: Ram is telling Sugriva what it means to be a real friend. They have just made a pact by a fire. Ram says a true friend turns you back from the wrong path, speaks of your strengths, and keeps your faults private. They treat your trouble as bigger than their own. They do not force their way in. They steer you right. They make sure your good parts are known. They keep your mistakes to themselves. This is what a friend does when the world has pushed you out.
verse.for_you: Your mind is telling you that vanishing would solve the noise. A friend would hear that scream and turn you back from the edge. They would name the good parts of you that you cannot see right now. They would keep your faults to themselves.
verse.try_today: Reach out to one person and tell them exactly what you feel right now.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting by the fire with a friend who sees you clearly.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
verse.line: See yourself in every being and every being in yourself, and you see the same everywhere.
verse.translation: One whose self is joined in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self; he sees the same everywhere.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna is showing Arjuna how to settle the mind through meditation. He tells him to see himself in every living being and every living being in himself. This is not a trick. It is a way to stop the mind from running away by giving it a single place to rest. When the mind wanders, which it will, the practice is to bring it back gently, again and again, and to feel the joy and sorrow of others as your own.
verse.for_you: You feel erased because your mind is spinning in a place where nothing holds. The noise you cannot stop is the mind looking for a place to land. You do not have to fight the thoughts today. Just notice them as they pass, like clouds. You are still here.
verse.try_today: Watch one thing move, like a leaf or a cloud, and let your mind rest on it for a minute.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting in a quiet room, and the mind will not stop looking for a door.

story.title: Rama comes home from his pilgrimage and loses interest in everything
story.story_hook: The prince who had everything came back from his travels and stopped laughing.
story.summary: Sixteen-year-old Rama returns from a long pilgrimage and quietly withdraws: he stops eating properly, stops laughing, ignores his duties and sits alone. His attendants tell the worried king. Vishvamitra and Vasishtha say this is not illness or weakness but the first stirring of real questions, and ask that Rama be brought to them.
story.lesson: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.

anchor.speaker: Rama's attendant
anchor.setting: Rama's attendants tell King Dasharatha how the prince has changed since his pilgrimage.
anchor.sanskrit: रामो राजीवपत्राक्षो यतःप्रभृति चागतः । सविप्रस्तीर्थयात्रायास्ततःप्रभृति दुर्मनाः ॥
anchor.line: Ever since he came back from the trip, he hasn't been himself.
anchor.translation: Ever since lotus-eyed Rama came back from his pilgrimage with the brahmins, he has been low in spirit.
anchor.why: Losing interest in everything can be the start of asking better questions, if someone helps you through it.
